title: the CI shards are balanced by time in one unit: a suite measured at zero seconds is fast, not unknown, and an unknown suite's estimate is in seconds
acceptance: Why. T-134 made CI parallel, but main's runs still take 7.5-9.5 minutes against a 10-minute job limit. On main 9e4194d the four bash shards held 1, 1, 1 and 31 suites: shards 1-3 ran tests/skills.test.sh, tests/protocol.test.sh and tests/lib.test.sh alone (about 10 s each) and shard 4 ran everything else (9m13s). Root cause, found by firstmate in bin/ci.sh ci_suite_duration: timings are recorded in whole seconds, the three fast suites were recorded as 0, `[ "$n" -gt 0 ]` then treats them as unknown and falls back to their byte size (thousands), so longest-first packing sees them as the three longest suites and gives each its own shard. Two units, seconds and bytes, are mixed in one sort. Its own spec file, design/tasks/T-148.json, is committed on this branch.

One unit. Timings are recorded with sub-second resolution (milliseconds); a suite present in the timings with any value, zero included, uses that value; a suite absent from them is estimated in the same unit (for example the median recorded duration per byte times its size), never raw bytes next to seconds.

Balanced. With the timings of the last main run, no shard's predicted load exceeds the mean by more than the longest single suite; a test feeds recorded timings with zeros and missing entries and checks the assignment. Wall-clock time of main's required check after this merges is reported from real runs; the target is under 4 minutes, and if the longest single suite alone exceeds that, the report names it (for T-130 to split).
Evidence: the required GitHub check and the gates, checked by firstmate at the merge gate. Workers do not run the suites themselves.
